# Managed Codex protocol fixtures

Synthetic samples of the Codex app-server stdio JSON-RPC contract that
Conflux's managed executor is built against. All text is fabricated; no user
session data is included.

- Generated by: `codex app-server generate-ts --out <tmp>` (2026-11-12)
- CLI version: `codex-cli 0.164.0` (Windows, npm install at `C:\nvm4w\nodejs\codex.cmd`)
- Cross-checked against the local codex source checkout at `5c3ff1dabf644169f4bd74b215719f381e4fdb3f`

The supported server version for the first managed-codex milestone is 0.164.0.
Incompatible versions must be rejected explicitly (initialize response carries
`userAgent`, which is where the server version is read back).

## Files

- `responses.json` — client request responses: initialize, thread/start, turn/start, plus a JSON-RPC error frame.
- `notifications.json` — server notifications for one successful turn lifecycle: thread/started, turn/started, item/started, item/agentMessage/delta, item/completed, turn/completed.
- `approval-requests.json` — item-based approval server requests (commandExecution, fileChange) plus the legacy pre-item variants, so transports can be tested against both generations.
- `failure-terminal.json` — failed and interrupted terminal turn payloads and the standalone `error` notification.

## Shape notes that matter to the transport

- Every server frame is a single JSON object per line (JSONL over stdio); request ids are echoed by the server.
- `thread/resume` documents rejoin semantics for running threads — a non-empty `path` is treated as a consistency check against the active rollout, which is how "thread owned by another host" surfaces.
- History verification should page via `thread/turns/list` + `thread/items/list`; `thread/read`'s `includeTurns` is deprecated for paginated threads.
- `item/commandExecution/requestApproval` decisions include amendment variants (`acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment`, `applyNetworkPolicyAmendment`); the first-milestone UI only ever answers `accept`, `decline`, or `cancel`.
